How do WE help voat succeed?

If you're moderating a subverse, clearly lay out and define your rules to remove ambiguity.

Downvoat circlejerky comments in serious discussion threads (e.g. Lenny faces, reaction images, etc.) and don't upvoat the easy jokes just because you're havin' a giggle. The occasional pun thread is nice, but having 9/10 of the top-level comments as jokes every time is not conducive to discussion.

Keep spreading the word, but don't do it in a spammy way or you'll turn people off quickly. Remember to interact with new users in /v/introductions and help ease their transition.

If you know C#, consider contributing to Voat's source code.

Lastly, if you're going to re-post content from Reddit/Imgur, do so only if you find interest in the content, and do some basic fact-checking instead of just copying the (usually) clickbait titles. "I thank you for the report, but I assure you that my castle is well defended. No army has gotten past our defenses in centuries, and certainly no lone man has even made it past the gate." The King preaches from atop his throne in a luxurious medieval throne room. Banners, tapestries, and beautiful vignettes hang from the walls illuminated by a few windows and plentiful torches.

"I still urge caution, your majesty. She is no ordinary person, if she could even be called that. She'd be more akin to a witch." The Dandy Man deeply contemplates his words, his white gloved hands running his chin as he thinks. His colorful ensemble of dress makes him stick out like a sore thumb, with the only matching colors being his gloves and fine white leather shoes.

"Woman or witch, it doesn't matter. Nobody is breaching our security!" The King slams his fist down on the armrest of his throne, an embittered tone rising from this throat. "Now, is this all the business that you have?"

An absolute terror. That is all that the royal guard can think as he is paralyzed not by fear or injury, but because the local physics have suddenly changed so as to disallow movement. He can feel the burning deep in his chest as his diaphragm is stuck and the carbon dioxide levels build up in his bleed. A bizarre itching sensation covers his body as his body produces sweat from fear, but the glands are unable to squeeze it out so instead just slowly flows out. But that is just a trifling matter to the cloaked figure who is approaching him in haste -- the one who annulled physics. Not that the guard even knows about physics, nor is it a good time for him to learn.

The cloaked figure reaches the guard and punches a hand into the chest. There is no sensation, even after the figure retracts their hand and pulls out a pile of glowing strings that look like wet yarn. White, blue, and even a little green. The figure sneers at the string, and for a moment the guard is able to see her face: A beautiful visage that is distorted by anger and irritation. Instantaneously as the threads hit the ground, the guard vanishes from existence and from having ever existed. Even the soul has ceased to have been.

"Halt! Who trespresses in these halls?" Another royal guard has entered the corridor when the cloaked enigma strands.

"Who trespasses? Only I, the unstoppable force." The cloaked figure presses her hand against the stone castle walls and slides her hand as if she was spinning a wheel. She continues walking towards the second guard as the hallway becomes secured in a new pocket dimension, and tumbles and rolls around like it was spinning down a cliff. The guard is unable to secure his footing and is tossed around like a ragdoll and is mercilessly ravaged by tapestries, rugs, torches, and other items as they topple in the careening corridor.

Just as soon as the corridor spirals, it comes to an abrupt stop as the pocket dimension snaps back into normal reality. The cloaked figure is next to the guard, and extends a shadowy and picks him up with ease by the breast of his jacket. Again she reaches inside of him and pulls out a tangling mess of glowing threads, but these have a slightly different pattern of coloration to them. The guard senses an opportunity as the figure is distracted by the mass and strikes at her with his spear, but his weapon and himself vaporize into non-existence before touching her.

"Did you hear that?" The King interrupts The Dandy Man. It was almost certain that everyone in the castle heard it, as the entire structure shuddered and groaned as a result of a side corridor being violently rerouted to the throne room entrance. Parts of the east wing collapsed as important supporting walls suddenly vanished in the unscheduled renovation.

"Oh dear." The Dandy Man covers his face in boredom. "Well, I did warn your Majesty that a witch was coming." He bows and tips his brilliant magenta top hat before walking over to a window facing the courtyard. There are no signs of life outside. There are no signs that there ever used to be life outside. "I guess this is where we part ways. Toodles!" He gives a defiantly mocking gesture before leaping from the window, hat under his arm to protect it.

The King sits in absolute shock. Various feelings well up inside of him: anger, rage, annoyance, betrayal. Even a strong undercurrent of fear. A feeling he is trying to suppress, as he tries to think to call a guard, any guard, but he can't remember hiring any. Strange, he was sure that he had hired plenty. His concerned contemplation over his lack of staff at his castle is quickly interrupted by a cloaked figure bursting into the throne room.

"I suppose you are the witch I have heard about." The King greets the cloaked figure.

"Is that what he is calling me? I guess that is a fair if unimpressive metaphor."

"Who are you, and what is your business here? Why do you trespass here?" The King musters all of his courage to say this in as neutral of a tone as possible. Every synapse in his brain is screaming for him to either run or fight, but he strains incredibly to maintain composure. Looking upon the figure before him, he knows innately that she isn't a witch but something of a much more awing persuasion.

"You're very inquisitive. I like that. I like that a lot." She shudders her body a bit and the cloak disappears into shadows which engulf her body as she transforms to her native form: a sleek and agile nightmare that would make the most epic of Lovecraftian horrors go mad in her presence. "I am the fourth Wandereur, Kynezjychk. I am the spirit of movement, motion, and direction. I am more than you can dare to comprehend with your material brain. But most importantly to you, I am your judge, jury, and executioner." A ghastly grin covers her face which bathes the King in a grisly light and obliterates his robes and coverings. Around the King's neck is a straight spring where both ends connect to each other, which Kyne grabs.

"A foolish King who sought everything for himself. Conquered many lands, subjugated many peoples. Your selfishness and hubris has damned you to purgatory." With every word that Kyne speaks, the Loop glows brighter and brighter. "This item which you claimed for yourself shall bear witness against you. Strange that you should lose, because if this item had been shared, then everything would be fine." The Loop reaches its maximum.

"Execute me for having possession of an item? What madness is this?" The King yelps. By now he is so overwhelmed by terror that any semblance of composure he had is gone.

"That which is meant to be shared was never shared. An item that brings good luck for one day, and asks that after that it be given to somebody new come morning. You murdered for this item, and coveted it. You did not just merely abuse it; you demeaned it." With a blast of energy, the Loop vanishes the King's right arm.

"Share? It is my divine right as King to secure treasures!" He scowls as he clutches at the open wound with his remaining arm, trying to stop the blood loss.

"You lack humility. You truly believe that God chose you to safeguard an item meant to be shared? You really believe that God asked you to ignore a lesson of humility and brotherhood, and hoard a trinket to yourself? You actually believe that you are any more special than anyone else in this reality, or that your precious little kingdom has any significance beyond its boundaries? You are tiny. Insignificant." The Loop shoots out two beams and vanishes the King's legs.

"I... I acted for the best interests of my people! With good luck, we could have been prosperous!" An urgent and panicked tone enters the King's vocal register.

"Lies. You used the luck you got on the first day to help yourself exclusively, and once it ran out after the first day you were selfish and decided to keep it for yourself, so you put it on a necklace so it would always be in your possession. If you truly had cared, you would not have acted selfishly." The Loop fires off three beams which vanish the remaining arm, the body, and the head. All that remains of the King now is his soul: a glowing spherical orb that shimmers in a collage of colorful light.

"Fine. I admit it! I am selfish. I squelched a treasure for myself at the expense of my people."

"And that is why you shall be the harbinger of Death." A shadow wraps around the King's soul and corrupts it. "Your kingdom, your planet, your cosmos. People you know, people you don't know, and people you never even conceived of existing shall perish with you because your sole actions have proven that your people are too dangerous to be gifted the last freedom."

Kyne slams the Loop into the King's soul, which detonates the corrupted soul into a wave of non-existence and spreads out from the area at speeds faster than light. Time and space across a variety of dimensions are shredded and disintegrated as the laws of physics and even mathematics and logic break down and crumble. It will take a few hours for the destruction wave to completely propagate to all regions of existence in this failed domain, but Kyne's work is done and she leaves. Her home domain once suffered such a fate; one only given to those domains whose inhabitants prove too dangerous to be allowed to interact with others. Countless realities extinguished so that they could be safe from the countless others who are capable of prospering and growing.

The only law that realities are judged against is to simply "Be kind."
